claim: Zcwpw1 is the most correlated gene with Prdm9 in single-cell meiosis analysis (rho = 0.519, p-value=2E-6).
source: As expected, the top Prdm9-correlated genes are known factors in spermatogenesis or DNA metabolism (Figure 1A, Figure 1—source data 1), however the most correlated gene in our analysis was Zcwpw1 (rho = 0.519, p-value=2E-6).
evidence: The claim is supported by single-cell RNA-sequencing data analysis showing correlation coefficients and p-values.

claim: Zcwpw1 mRNA is highly expressed exclusively in the testis in both mouse and human.
source: Similar to Prdm9, Zcwpw1 mRNA is highly expressed exclusively in the testis in both mouse and human (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A–B).
evidence: The claim is supported by expression data shown in supplementary figures.

claim: ZCWPW1 expression is mostly restricted to the testis in mice.
source: We confirmed that ZCWPW1 expression is mostly restricted to the testis in mice (Figure 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by Western blot data showing tissue-specific expression.

claim: Mouse ZCWPW1 has three recognizable domains: SCP1, zf-CW and PWWP.
source: Mouse ZCWPW1 has three recognizable domains from the NCBI conserved domain (CD) database: SCP1, zf-CW and PWWP (Figure 1C).
evidence: The claim is based on bioinformatics analysis using NCBI conserved domain database.

claim: The PWWP domain binds specifically to histone H3 containing the H3K36me3 mark.
source: The PWWP domain found in multiple proteins binds specifically to histone H3 containing the H3K36me3 mark (Qin and Min, 2014)
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to published literature.

claim: The zf-CW domain of ZCWPW1 possesses H3K4me3-specific binding activity.
source: while the zf-CW domain of ZCWPW1 was found to possess H3K4me3-specific binding activity (He et al., 2010).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to published literature.

claim: The SCP1 domain has homology to the synaptonemal complex protein 1 (SYCP1).
source: The SCP1 domain has homology to the synaptonemal complex protein 1 (SYCP1), the major component of the transverse filaments of the synaptonemal complex (de Vries et al., 2005).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to published literature.

claim: The N-terminal region of SYCP1 homologous to the SCP1 domain of ZCWPW1 plays a role in SYCP1 dimerization that facilitates synaptonemal complex assembly.
source: The N-terminal region of SYCP1 homologous to the SCP1 domain of ZCWPW1 plays a role in SYCP1 dimerization that facilitates synaptonemal complex assembly (Seo et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to published literature.

claim: The NCBI CD database does not recognize the SCP1-like domain in other ZCWPW1 orthologs, including human.
source: It is notable that the NCBI CD database does not recognize the SCP1-like domain in other ZCWPW1 orthologs, including human (Figure 1C).
evidence: The claim is based on bioinformatics analysis using NCBI conserved domain database.

claim: Recombinant ZCWPW1 binds with higher affinity to H3K4me3 and H3K36me3 than non-methylated biotinylated H3 peptides.
source: Using in vitro biotin-streptavidin pulldown assays, we determined that recombinant ZCWPW1 (residues 1–440) binds with higher affinity to H3K4me3 and H3K36me3 than non-methylated biotinylated H3 peptides (Figure 1D).
evidence: The claim is supported by in vitro binding assay data.

claim: Dual-modified H3K4me3/K36me3 peptides had the highest binding affinity for ZCWPW1 compared to peptides with either single modification.
source: Importantly, dual-modified H3K4me3/K36me3 peptides had the highest binding affinity for ZCWPW1 compared to peptides with either single modification (Figure 1D).
evidence: The claim is supported by in vitro binding assay data.

claim: ZCWPW1 binds with the highest affinity to H3K4me3/K36me3 peptides (KD = 1.7 ± 0.3 µM) compared to H3K4me3 or H3K36me3 alone (KD >10 µM each), with a 1:1 stoichiometry.
source: We further quantified the binding of ZCWPW1 to histone peptides by Isothermal Titration Calorimetry, which demonstrated that ZCWPW1 binds with the highest affinity to H3K4me3/K36me3 peptides (KD = 1.7 ± 0.3 µM) compared to H3K4me3 or H3K36me3 alone (KD >10 µM each), with a 1:1 stoichiometry (Figure 1E).
evidence: The claim is supported by isothermal titration calorimetry measurements.

claim: ZCWPW1 is a meiosis specific histone methylation reader for the unique dual methyl marks catalyzed by PRDM9.
source: In sum these results indicate that ZCWPW1 is a meiosis specific histone methylation reader for the unique dual methyl marks catalyzed by PRDM9, suggesting that ZCWPW1 and PRDM9 have complementary roles in meiosis.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the binding data and expression patterns.

claim: PRDM9 has a rapidly evolving zinc finger array leading to distinct hotspots even among species belonging to the same genus.
source: PRDM9 has an extraordinary evolutionary pattern as it possesses a rapidly evolving zinc finger array leading to distinct hotspots even among species belonging to the same genus (Baker et al., 2017; Oliver et al., 2009; Thomas et al., 2009).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: PRDM9 emerged in jawless fishes and has been repeatedly lost in several species across different clades including in birds, crocodiles, and amphibians, as well as in several lineages of fish.
source: Furthermore, while it emerged in jawless fishes, it has been repeatedly lost in several species across different clades including in birds, crocodiles, and amphibians, as well as in several lineages of fish.
evidence: The claim is based on evolutionary analysis of PRDM9 across species.

claim: 174 vertebrate species with ZCWPW1 were identified from databases.
source: Using this strategy, we identified 174 vertebrate species with ZCWPW1 (Figure 2—source data 1).
evidence: The claim is based on database searches and motif analysis.

claim: An additional 19 species with ZCWPW1 orthologs were identified using BLAST approach.
source: Using this approach, we identified an additional 19 species with ZCWPW1 orthologs (Figure 2—source data 1).
evidence: The claim is based on BLAST searches and phylogenetic analysis.

claim: Both the zf-CW and PWWP domains of ZCWPW1 are highly conserved.
source: Next, we looked for sequence conservation of ZCWPW1 by performing multiple sequence alignment of all identified orthologs. Both the zf-CW and PWWP domains are highly conserved (Figure 2A, Figure 2B, Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple sequence alignment analysis.

claim: The N-terminal region corresponding to the SCP1 domain in mouse ZCWPW1 showed weaker but detectable conservation.
source: Furthermore, the N-terminal region corresponding to the SCP1 domain in mouse ZCWPW1 showed weaker but detectable conservation.
evidence: The claim is supported by sequence alignment analysis.

claim: The SCP1 domain of mouse ZCWPW1 has 30% identity with SCP1 domain of mouse SYCP1.
source: When we aligned the SCP1 domain of mouse ZCWPW1 with SCP1 domain of mouse SYCP1 (Figure 2—figure supplement 3A), we observed 30% identity.
evidence: The claim is supported by sequence alignment analysis.

claim: No birds or crocodile species with Zcwpw1 orthologs were identified, similar to Prdm9.
source: Interestingly, we could not identify any birds or crocodile species with Zcwpw1 orthologs, similar to Prdm9 (Baker et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is based on database searches and evolutionary analysis.

claim: Some amphibians and dogs have Zcwpw1 orthologs, unlike Prdm9.
source: However, unlike Prdm9, some amphibians and dogs have Zcwpw1 orthologs (Figure 2—source data 1).
evidence: The claim is based on database searches and evolutionary analysis.

claim: All species with both Prdm9 and Zcwpw1 orthologs maintained the three catalytic tyrosine residues of PRDM9.
source: Strikingly, we found that all species with both Prdm9 and Zcwpw1 orthologs maintained the three catalytic tyrosine residues of PRDM9, whereas the three catalytic tyrosines were present in only 3 out of 29 species lacking Zcwpw1 orthologs (Figure 2C).
evidence: The claim is supported by sequence analysis of PRDM9 catalytic residues across species.

claim: 4,487 ZCWPW1 peaks were identified (p<0.001) in mouse spermatocytes.
source: We identified 4,487 ZCWPW1 peaks (p<0.001).
evidence: The claim is supported by CUT&RUN sequencing data and peak calling analysis.

claim: 89% of ZCWPW1 peaks overlap with previously identified hotspots defined by the presence of DMC1.
source: Most ZCWPW1 peaks overlap with previously identified hotspots defined by the presence of the single-strand (ss) DNA binding protein DMC1 (Brick et al., 2018; Figure 3A) or released SPO11-oligos (Lange et al., 2016; Figure 3—figure supplement 1A) (89% and 58% respectively).
evidence: The claim is supported by comparison of ZCWPW1 CUT&RUN data with published DMC1 SSDS data.

claim: 58% of ZCWPW1 peaks overlap with released SPO11-oligos.
source: Most ZCWPW1 peaks overlap with previously identified hotspots defined by the presence of the single-strand (ss) DNA binding protein DMC1 (Brick et al., 2018; Figure 3A) or released SPO11-oligos (Lange et al., 2016; Figure 3—figure supplement 1A) (89% and 58% respectively).
evidence: The claim is supported by comparison of ZCWPW1 CUT&RUN data with published SPO11-oligo data.

claim: ZCWPW1 signal exhibits positive correlation with SPO11-oligo density, DMC1-SSDS and PRDM9 binding signals.
source: Additionally, ZCWPW1 signal exhibits positive correlation with SPO11-oligo density, DMC1-SSDS and PRDM9 binding signals (Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by correlation analysis of ZCWPW1 signal with other recombination metrics.

claim: PRDM9 binding generates a nucleosome-depleted region with nucleosomes organized symmetrically around PRDM9 binding sites.
source: PRDM9 binding generates a nucleosome-depleted region with nucleosomes organized symmetrically around PRDM9 binding sites (Baker et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to published literature.

claim: Only 8%, 9% and 5% of ZCWPW1 called peaks overlap with TSS, TES and CGI respectively.
source: Next, we looked for ZCWPW1 overlap with functional regions in the genome: Transcription Start Sites (TSS), Transcription End Sites (TES) and CpG islands (CGI), and we found only 8%, 9% and 5% of our ZCWPW1 called peaks overlap with these sites respectively (Figure 3—figure supplement 3B).
evidence: The claim is supported by genomic overlap analysis of ZCWPW1 peaks.

claim: There was no significant ZCWPW1 enrichment genome-wide at TSS, TES, and CGI compared to IgG control.
source: Despite ZCWPW1 peaks overlapping with these sites, there was no significant ZCWPW1 enrichment genome-wide in these functional sites compared to IgG control (Figure 3—figure supplement 3A, Figure 3—figure supplement 3C).
evidence: The claim is supported by comparison of ZCWPW1 signal to IgG control at functional genomic sites.

claim: 85% of ZCWPW1 peaks overlapped with regions containing both H3K4me3 and H3K36me3 marks.
source: The vast majority of ZCWPW1 peaks overlapped with regions containing both H3K4me3 and H3K36me3 marks (85%), with significantly less peaks overlapping with regions marked by either mark alone (Figure 3C, Figure 3D).
evidence: The claim is supported by overlap analysis of ZCWPW1 peaks with histone modification ChIP-seq data.

claim: ZCWPW1 CUT&RUN signals are significantly stronger in peaks with H3K4me3/H3K36me3 dual marks compared to regions with a single mark.
source: In agreement with in vitro binding assays (Figure 1D, Figure 1E), we found that ZCWPW1 CUT&RUN signals are significantly stronger in peaks with H3K4me3/H3K36me3 dual marks compared to regions with a single mark (Figure 3C).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative analysis of ZCWPW1 signal strength at different histone modification states.

claim: No enrichment of ZCWPW1 relative to control was observed in the pseudo-autosomal region (PAR) of sex chromosomes.
source: Finally, we did not observe any enrichment of ZCWPW1 relative to control in the pseudo-autosomal region (PAR) of sex chromosomes, which undergoes PRDM9-independent recombination in mice (Brick et al., 2012; Figure 3—figure supplement 4).
evidence: The claim is supported by analysis of ZCWPW1 signal at PAR region compared to control.

claim: Motif analysis identified exclusively the PRDM9 binding motif of the Dom2 allele (PRDM9Dom2) within ZCWPW1 peak regions (p=1e-261).
source: This analysis identified exclusively the PRDM9 binding motif of the Dom2 allele (PRDM9Dom2), found within the C57Bl/6J strain (p=1e-261) (Figure 4—source data 1), suggesting that ZCWPW1 occupancy is solely PRDM9-dependent.
evidence: The claim is supported by de novo motif discovery analysis of ZCWPW1 peaks.

claim: 8,976 ZCWPW1 peaks were identified in F1-hybrid mouse spermatocytes from a C57Bl/6J (B6) and CAST/EiJ (CAST) cross.
source: In these mice, we identified 8,976 peaks, 60% of which overlap with previously described CAST/CAST hotspots (Smagulova et al., 2016), while only 18% overlap with B6/B6 hotspots (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A), a finding consistent with reported PRDM9Cast dominance in hybrid mice (Baker et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by CUT&RUN data from F1-hybrid mice.

claim: 60% of ZCWPW1 peaks in F1-hybrid mice overlap with previously described CAST/CAST hotspots.
source: In these mice, we identified 8,976 peaks, 60% of which overlap with previously described CAST/CAST hotspots (Smagulova et al., 2016), while only 18% overlap with B6/B6 hotspots (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A), a finding consistent with reported PRDM9Cast dominance in hybrid mice (Baker et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by overlap analysis of ZCWPW1 peaks with published hotspot data.

claim: 18% of ZCWPW1 peaks in F1-hybrid mice overlap with B6/B6 hotspots.
source: In these mice, we identified 8,976 peaks, 60% of which overlap with previously described CAST/CAST hotspots (Smagulova et al., 2016), while only 18% overlap with B6/B6 hotspots (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A), a finding consistent with reported PRDM9Cast dominance in hybrid mice (Baker et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by overlap analysis of ZCWPW1 peaks with published hotspot data.

claim: ZCWPW1 binds to 1,383 novel hotspots that do not exist in either B6/B6 or CAST/CAST mice, but only appear in F1-hybrids.
source: Furthermore, ZCWPW1 also binds to 1,383 novel hotspots that do not exist in either B6/B6 or CAST/CAST mice, but only appear in F1-hybrids, where PRDM9Cast binds to the B6 genome and PRDM9Dom2 binds to the CAST genome (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by analysis of ZCWPW1 peaks unique to F1-hybrid mice.

claim: De novo motif discovery in the hybrids revealed two motifs identical to PRDM9Cast and PRDM9Dom2 (p=1e-768 and 1e-60 respectively).
source: De novo motif discovery in the hybrids revealed two motifs identical to PRDM9Cast and PRDM9Dom2 (p=1e-768 and 1e-60 respectively) (Figure 4A; Figure 4—source data 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by de novo motif discovery analysis of ZCWPW1 peaks in F1-hybrid mice.

claim: ZCWPW1 occupancy is a novel marker for meiotic hotspots that reflects PRDM9 allele specificity.
source: Overall, these results indicate that ZCWPW1 occupancy is a novel marker for meiotic hotspots that reflects PRDM9 allele specificity, and ZCWPW1 CUT&RUN is a useful method to infer PRDM9 binding sites.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the allele-specific binding patterns of ZCWPW1.

claim: Zcwpw1 KO mice were born healthy and at mendelian ratios.
source: To test that hypothesis, we generated mice with homozygous deletion of Zcwpw1 (Zcwpw1 KO), which were born healthy and at mendelian ratios.
evidence: The claim is based on observation of Zcwpw1 KO mice.

claim: Zcwpw1 KO testes are smaller and have reduced mass (80 mg vs.190 mg) compared to wild type.
source: Western blotting confirmed the absence of ZCWPW1 in testis from Zcwpw1 KO mice (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A), which are smaller and have reduced mass (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B) compared to wild type (Zcwpw1 WT) (80 mg vs.190 mg).
evidence: The claim is supported by measurement of testis mass in WT and KO mice.

claim: Zcwpw1 KO testes show total absence of spermatids in the seminiferous tubules.
source: Hematoxylin and Eosin (H&E) staining of tissue sections demonstrated the total absence of spermatids in the seminiferous tubules of Zcwpw1 KO testes (Figure 5A and Figure 5—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: The claim is supported by histological analysis of testis sections.

claim: Zcwpw1 KO mice arrest at a pachytene-like stage of prophase I.
source: SYCP3/SYCP1 staining revealed that Zcwpw1 KO mice arrest at a pachytene-like stage of prophase I (Figure 5B).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence staining of spermatocyte spreads.

claim: Almost all spermatocytes in Zcwpw1 KO mice displayed partial chromosomal asynapsis.
source: In Zcwpw1 KO mice, almost all spermatocytes displayed partial chromosomal asynapsis (Figure 5C), with an average of 12 autosomal chromosomes synapsed per spermatocyte (out of 19), in contrast to Zcwpw1 WT spermatocytes which -with rare exceptions- have all homologous autosomal chromosomes fully synapsed in spermatocytes at the pachytene stage (Figure 5D).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantification of synapsed chromosomes in spermatocyte spreads.

claim: Zcwpw1 KO spermatocytes have an average of 12 autosomal chromosomes synapsed per spermatocyte (out of 19).
source: In Zcwpw1 KO mice, almost all spermatocytes displayed partial chromosomal asynapsis (Figure 5C), with an average of 12 autosomal chromosomes synapsed per spermatocyte (out of 19), in contrast to Zcwpw1 WT spermatocytes which -with rare exceptions- have all homologous autosomal chromosomes fully synapsed in spermatocytes at the pachytene stage (Figure 5D).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantification of synapsed chromosomes in spermatocyte spreads.

claim: Spermatocytes from Zcwpw1 KO mice have widespread focal accumulation of DMC1 in the cells arrested at pachytene-like stage.
source: Spermatocytes from Zcwpw1 KO mice have widespread focal accumulation of DMC1 in the cells arrested at pachytene-like stage (Figure 5E), with significantly increased numbers of DMC1 foci per spermatocyte in Zcwpw1 KO (Figure 5F).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence staining and quantification of DMC1 foci.

claim: Zcwpw1 KO spermatocytes have significantly increased numbers of DMC1 foci per spermatocyte.
source: Spermatocytes from Zcwpw1 KO mice have widespread focal accumulation of DMC1 in the cells arrested at pachytene-like stage (Figure 5E), with significantly increased numbers of DMC1 foci per spermatocyte in Zcwpw1 KO (Figure 5F).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantification of DMC1 foci in spermatocyte spreads.

claim: γ-H2AX staining showed significant accumulation on autosomes and the absence of the XY sex body in Zcwpw1 KO spermatocytes.
source: Furthermore, γ-H2AX staining showed significant accumulation on autosomes and the absence of the XY sex body, indicating prophase blockage before sex body formation (Figure 5—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence staining of spermatocyte spreads.

claim: Zcwpw1 KO spermatocytes have pachytene-like meiotic arrest with partial asynapsis and increased DMC1 foci compared to Zcwpw1 WT spermatocytes.
source: Our observations from immunofluorescence staining are in agreement with what has been recently reported by two different groups who found that Zcwpw1 KO spermatocytes have pachytene-like meiotic arrest with partial asynapsis and increased DMC1 foci compared to Zcwpw1 WT spermatocytes (Li et al., 2019a; Wells et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by the authors' data and citations to other published studies.

claim: Zcwpw1 KO mice phenocopy Prdm9 null male mice in which sperm production is compromised by partially defective DSB repair and synapsis with meiotic arrest at a pachytene-like stage.
source: Collectively, Zcwpw1 KO mice phenocopy Prdm9 null male mice in which sperm production is compromised by partially defective DSB repair and synapsis with meiotic arrest at a pachytene-like stage (Brick et al., 2012; Hayashi et al., 2005).
evidence: The claim is based on comparison of Zcwpw1 KO phenotype with published Prdm9 KO phenotype.

claim: In Prdm9-null male mice, meiotic DSBs reposition away from PRDM9 bound motifs to promoters and at other sites of PRDM9-independent H3K4me3.
source: In Prdm9-null male mice, meiotic DSBs reposition away from PRDM9 bound motifs to promoters and at other sites of PRDM9-independent H3K4me3 (Brick et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to published literature.

claim: END-seq identified 2,098 and 3,147 DSB sites in spermatocytes from Zcwpw1 WT and Zcwpw1 KO mice respectively.
source: Peak calling on END-seq reads identified 2,098 and 3,147 DSB sites in spermatocytes from Zcwpw1 WT and Zcwpw1 KO mice respectively.
evidence: The claim is supported by END-seq data and peak calling analysis.

claim: DSBs in Zcwpw1 KO mice nearly completely overlapped with DSBs in Zcwpw1 WT.
source: Surprisingly, unlike the case in Prdm9 KO, DSBs in Zcwpw1 KO mice nearly completely overlapped with DSBs in Zcwpw1 WT, and with previously identified hotpots in B6 mice using DMC1 SSDS (Figure 6A, Figure 6B, Figure 6C).
evidence: The claim is supported by overlap analysis of END-seq peaks between WT and KO.

claim: Unlike in Prdm9 KO mice, DSBs in Zcwpw1 KO were not repositioned towards promoters.
source: Importantly, unlike in Prdm9 KO mice, DSBs were not repositioned towards promoters (Figure 6B).
evidence: The claim is supported by END-seq data showing DSB distribution at promoters.

claim: ZCWPW1 is not required for the positioning of DSBs, rather it is required exclusively for efficient DSB repair and homologous recombination.
source: In sum these data indicate that unlike PRDM9, ZCWPW1 is not required for the positioning of DSBs, rather it is required exclusively for efficient DSB repair and homologous recombination.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the END-seq data showing DSB positioning is unchanged in Zcwpw1 KO.

claim: PRDM9 is a unique SET domain containing histone methyltransferase that contains its own specific DNA binding domain, a rapidly evolving C2H2 zinc finger array.
source: PRDM9 is a unique SET domain containing histone methyltransferase in several respects. First, it contains its own specific DNA binding domain, a rapidly evolving C2H2 zinc finger array that binds to target sequences with high specificity.
evidence: The claim is based on established knowledge about PRDM9 structure and function.

claim: PRDM9 contains a dual specificity histone methyltransferase activity for histone H3 K4 and histone H3 K36.
source: Second, it contains a dual specificity histone methyltransferase activity for histone H3 K4 and histone H3 K36 (Eram et al., 2014; Powers et al., 2016; Wu et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: ZCWPW1 is a unique protein that possesses dual histone methylation reader domains; a zf-CW domain that binds to the H3K4me3 mark, and a PWWP domain that binds to the H3K36me3 mark.
source: Likewise, ZCWPW1 is a unique protein that possesses dual histone methylation reader domains; a zf-CW domain that has previously been shown to bind to the H3K4me3 mark (He et al., 2010), and a PWWP domain, which has been shown on multiple proteins including DNMT3a and DNMT3b to bind to the H3K36me3 mark (Rondelet et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published literature about domain functions.

claim: ZCWPW1 can bind to histone H3 peptides with double H3K4me3 and H3K36me3 marks in vitro with high affinity at a 1:1 ratio.
source: ZCWPW1 can bind to histone H3 peptides with double H3K4me3 and H3K36me3 marks in vitro with high affinity at a 1:1 ratio.
evidence: The claim is supported by in vitro binding assays and ITC measurements.

claim: PRDM9 predominantly methylates H3K4me3 and H3K36me3 on the +1, +2,–1 and –2 nucleosomes flanking its binding sites.
source: Furthermore, PRDM9 predominantly methylates H3K4me3 and H3K36me3 on the +1, +2,–1 and –2 nucleosomes flanking its binding sites, which provides a short platform for ZCWPW1 interaction with chromatin at sites in vivo.
evidence: The claim is based on established knowledge about PRDM9 activity and inference about ZCWPW1 binding.

claim: ZCWPW1 is dispensable for initiating DSBs at PRDM9-bound hotspots.
source: Against our expectations, ZCWPW1 is dispensable for initiating DSBs at PRDM9-bound hotspots, as DSBs in Zcwpw1 KO male mice are still located at PRDM9 bound sites.
evidence: The claim is supported by END-seq data showing DSB positioning is unchanged in Zcwpw1 KO.

claim: ZCWPW1 is critical for the efficient repair of PRDM9-dependent breaks.
source: Our data instead suggests that ZCWPW1 is critical for the efficient repair of these PRDM9-dependent breaks.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the accumulation of DSB markers in Zcwpw1 KO mice.

claim: PRDM9 histone methyltransferase activity is essential for DSB formation at PRDM9 binding sites.
source: The findings that PRDM9 histone methyltransferase activity is essential for DSB formation at PRDM9 binding sites (Diagouraga et al., 2018; Powers et al., 2016) would therefore seem to suggest that a yet to be described PRDM9 histone methyl reader may link PRDM9 to the DSB machinery upstream of ZCWPW1.
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published literature and speculation about an unknown reader.

claim: ZCWPW2, a paralog of ZCWPW1 that diverged early in evolution, is a possible candidate for linking PRDM9 to the DSB machinery.
source: ZCWPW2, a paralog of ZCWPW1 that diverged early in evolution, is a possible candidate.
evidence: The claim is speculative based on evolutionary relationship between ZCWPW1 and ZCWPW2.

claim: In Zcwpw1 KO spermatocytes, the END-seq profile at hotspots demonstrates the presence of a central peak comparable to WT mice.
source: In Zcwpw1 KO spermatocytes, the END-seq profile at hotspots demonstrates the presence of a central peak comparable to WT mice.
evidence: The claim is supported by END-seq data analysis.

claim: Central peaks in END-seq are lost in Dmc1 KO mice which fail to undergo strand invasion.
source: Such central peaks are lost in Dmc1 KO mice which fail to undergo strand invasion (Paiano et al., 2020).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to published literature.

claim: ZCWPW1 functions as a PRDM9 specific synapsis factor that is necessary to bind both the cut and uncut homologs to link PRDM9-bound DNA loops to the SC, to facilitate later steps in meiotic recombination.
source: We propose a model in which ZCWPW1 functions as a PRDM9 specific synapsis factor that is necessary to bind both the cut and uncut homologs to link PRDM9-bound DNA loops to the SC, to facilitate later steps in meiotic recombination.
evidence: The claim is a proposed model based on the data presented.

claim: Symmetrical PRDM9 binding is critical for meiotic recombination.
source: This model is supported by a recent study which suggested that symmetrical PRDM9 binding is critical for meiotic recombination.
evidence: The claim is supported by reference to a recent study.

claim: The moderately conserved SCP1 domain found at the N-terminus of mouse ZCWPW1 shares homology to a region of the central axis protein SYCP1 that makes a coiled-coil and facilitates dimerization.
source: A hint may lie within the moderately conserved SCP1 domain found at the N-terminus of mouse ZCWPW1 which shares homology to a region of the central axis protein SYCP1 that makes a coiled-coil and facilitates dimerization (Seo et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is based on sequence homology and citation to published literature about SYCP1 function.

claim: PRDM9 bound loops could be directly tethered to the SC via ZCWPW1.
source: Thus, PRDM9 bound loops could be directly tethered to the SC via ZCWPW1.
evidence: The claim is speculative based on the SCP1 domain homology.

claim: END-seq is a method of directly sequencing DSBs that can be applied to a single mouse testis to map thousands of hotspots.
source: END-seq is a method of directly sequencing DSBs, and we have applied it to a single mouse testis to map thousands of hotspots.
evidence: The claim is based on the application of END-seq method in this study.

claim: ZCWPW1 CUT&RUN maps mouse hotspots by mapping the occupancy of ZCWPW1 that is directly downstream of PRDM9-induced histone methylation marks.
source: ZCWPW1 CUT&RUN also maps mouse hotspots, by mapping the occupancy of the factor ZCWPW1 that is directly downstream of PRDM9-induced histone methylation marks using a polyclonal antibody.
evidence: The claim is based on the application of ZCWPW1 CUT&RUN method in this study.

claim: ZCWPW1 occupancy correlates positively with the strength of hotspots in mice.
source: Importantly, ZCWPW1 occupancy correlates positively with the strength of hotspots in mice.
evidence: The claim is supported by correlation analysis of ZCWPW1 signal with hotspot metrics.

claim: ZCWPW1 CUT&RUN was applied to 300,000 bulk testicular cells from adult mice to sensitively map thousands of mouse hotspots.
source: We applied ZCWPW1 CUT&RUN to 300,000 bulk testicular cells from adult mice (a tiny fraction of the material obtained from a single adult testis) to sensitively map thousands of mouse hotspots.
evidence: The claim is based on the application of ZCWPW1 CUT&RUN method in this study.

claim: In yeast, plants and at least some vertebrates (those that lost PRDM9 like canids and birds), meiotic hotspots are located in the nucleosome free regions at gene promoters.
source: In yeast, plants and at least some vertebrates (those that lost PRDM9 like canids and birds); meiotic hotspots are located in the nucleosome free regions at gene promoters.
evidence: The claim is based on established knowledge from the literature.

claim: Within species that evolved PRDM9, hotspots are specified by the DNA binding activity of the PRDM9 zinc finger array.
source: However, within species that evolved PRDM9, hotspots are specified by the DNA binding activity of the PRDM9 zinc finger array.
evidence: The claim is based on established knowledge from the literature.

claim: The emergence of PRDM9 was a landmark that re-shaped patterns of meiotic recombination during evolution.
source: Therefore, the emergence of PRDM9 was a landmark that re-shaped patterns of meiotic recombination during evolution.
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the evolutionary analysis and functional data.
